title: Frequency-specific interaural crossing discordance does not improve transported tinnitus classification beyond standard audiometric summaries
abstract: We tested a nonnegative audiometric contrast: mean absolute interaural difference across five frequencies minus the absolute mean signed difference. It preserves frequency-specific crossing information absent from ear averages. Weighted logistic models trained in NHANES2011–2012 (3816 adults, 582 tinnitus cases) were frozen and evaluated in separately recruited NHANES2015–2016 (4262; 616 cases). Beyond demographics, better/worse speech-frequency averages, high-frequency hearing, PTA asymmetry and notch depth, weighted Brier score changed from 0.12258161 to 0.12283167, delta +0.00025006, joint rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.00018516,+0.00102696]. No incremental benefit was established; spline and full-frequency comparators also failed to show point benefit. This exploratory temporal-transport negative result is not equivalence, a causal result, or validation of a diagnostic tool.
